definition: In the plural phrase Ember Days, one of the quarterly sets of traditional Christian fast days; the September set follows Holy Cross Day, so September 16 is often Ember Wednesday.
etymology: This calendar word came through Old English ymbrendagas, “Ember days.” Its deeper origin is disputed: it has often been linked to Latin quattuor tempora, “the four seasons,” though the old English form may also reflect a native word for a circuit or recurring course. It is unrelated to the glowing remnant of a fire.
usage: The old almanac marked Ember Wednesday with a spare cross beside the harvest entries.
